paper_title: Checking Presence Reachability Properties on Parameterized Shared-Memory Systems

statement: It is unknown whether the previous result still holds when dim is fixed to a value greater than 1. The case dim = 1 is particularly easy because writing to the register completely erases its content.
context: The algorithm iteratively removes from P states that are not in C(P) ∩ BC(P). Indeed, states that are not in C(P) ∩ BC(P) cannot appear in any synchronizing execution. If it ends up with Q(P) = ∅, then there is no synchronizing execution and the algorithm rejects. If it ends up with C(P) = BC(P) = Q(P) ̸= ∅, then applying the definitions of C(P) and BC(P) gives a synchronizing execution, and the algorithm accepts. ◀ It is unknown whether the previous result still holds when dim is fixed to a value greater than 1. The case dim = 1 is particularly easy because writing to the register completely erases its content. Unlike COVER, TARGET and therefore DNF-PRP are not tractable under the uninitialized hypothesis. For TARGET, one cannot add fresh processes at no cost, since the fresh processes would eventually have to get to qf . For example, if a register r can only be written from a given state q, the last process to leave q will fix the value in register r. ▶ Proposition 13. TARGET for uninitialized roundless register protocols is NP-hard.
